reading.body:
H.R. 1788 has 18 Democratic sponsors and cosponsors and no recorded lobbying activity naming it since 2025.

The bill's support is entirely one-party. Maxwell Frost sponsors it, and every one of the 17 cosponsors is a Democrat. The bill's own text is tagged with bias and civil rights as its issues, which is how a grocery pricing measure lands in a dataset about AI governance. The status date is 2025-03-03, and no lobbying filing from 2025 or later names the bill.

The absence of lobbying filings is the notable fact. A bill that draws no named lobbying activity is not yet an issue that organized money is tracking, at least not in the filings captured here. The blurb is explicit that a filing naming a bill shows only that the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken, so even a future filing would not indicate support or opposition.

This data does not connect to compute, buildings, or power. It covers sponsorship, cosponsorship, issue tags, and lobbying mentions, and nothing about data centers, electricity demand, or AI infrastructure. The link to AI runs through the bias and civil rights tag alone, and the data does not explain what in the bill's text earned that tag.

summary: H.R. 1788, Fair Grocery Pricing Act. Latest status date 2025-03-03. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: bias and civil rights. 0 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
